source.title: Leveraging distillation token and weaker teacher model to improve DeiT transfer learning capability
source.authors: Christopher Gavra Reswara; Gede Putra Kusuma

record.file_problem: none; full article text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The article uses weak-to-strong generalization to motivate transfer-learning DeiT with a weaker teacher, but reports student performance rather than testing whether the student beats the weak teacher or recovers a performance gap.
record.gate_note: The article does not report standalone downstream-task accuracy for the teacher models or calculate PGR, so its comparisons cannot establish that the student beats its weak supervisor. It also compares soft with hard distillation and CNN with transformer teachers; those are method comparisons, not tests of student-versus-weak-supervisor performance.
record.test_reason: The study cites weak-to-strong generalization only to motivate using smaller CNN teachers for DeiT distillation. It is not a weak-to-strong test for three reasons. The student trains on ground-truth labels plus teacher logits (global loss averages true-label cross-entropy and distillation loss), not on weak labels alone. Teacher downstream accuracy is never reported. 'Weaker' is defined only by parameter count. All results compare student accuracy across teacher choices or loss types, so no result shows whether a student beats its weak supervisor or recovers a performance gap.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that distillation-token transfer learning improves DeiT on downstream datasets, that a CNN teacher with soft distillation works best, and that weaker (smaller) teachers give similar or sometimes better student accuracy while cutting teacher-training cost by about 75%.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses ImageNet-1k-pretrained DeiT students and teachers transferred to vision datasets. Student training combines true-label cross-entropy with teacher-logit distillation loss; the teacher is separately fine-tuned on the downstream dataset. This is not the original PGR evaluation. The study cites weak-to-strong generalization as motivation for using weaker teachers.
record.method_sensitivity: Student performance varies with teacher architecture and size, downstream dataset, student model, and hard versus soft distillation.

fits_no_version.finding: With true-label plus distillation training, smaller EfficientNet teachers gave DeiT student accuracy similar to or above a RegNet Y 16GF teacher. Examples: Pets with EfficientNet B4, 90.16% vs 90.73% (RegNet); Pets with EfficientNet V2S, +1.06%; Flowers with EfficientNet V2S, -0.42%; CIFAR-10 with EfficientNet B0 (DeiT S), 96.82% vs 96.89% (RegNet).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In DeiT transfer learning with a true-label loss plus distillation, a much smaller CNN teacher can yield student accuracy comparable to, or sometimes higher than, a larger CNN teacher; the result varies by dataset and student.

fits_no_version.finding: Soft distillation beat hard distillation, e.g. 95.83% vs 92.51% on Flowers and +1.34% on CIFAR-100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For DeiT distillation-token transfer learning, soft (KL) distillation outperforms hard distillation on task accuracy.

record.peer_reviewed: International Journal of Informatics and Communication Technology (IJ-ICT)
record.problems: Teacher-model downstream-task accuracy and PGR are not reported, preventing a direct test of whether the student beats its supervisor. Numerical results are supplied only for selected comparisons; many other comparisons are described qualitatively or shown in figures. No uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: Not recorded as rows: the CNN-versus-transformer teacher comparison and standard no-teacher comparisons in Sections 3.1 and 3.3, because they do not compare a weak supervisor with its student. Other values presented only graphically were not transcribed where the text supplied no condition-specific result.

untested.parts: No teacher downstream accuracy or PGR, and training includes ground-truth labels, so student-vs-weak-supervisor performance is untested.
Soft vs hard distillation is compared only on student accuracy with a similar-size teacher; no PGR against naive weak-label fine-tuning.
Teacher size and dataset vary, but no PGR or predictors of it are measured.
No exploitation, distribution-shift or shared-error analysis.
The setting is vision, but the weak-to-strong effect itself (student exceeding a weak supervisor trained on weak labels) is not measured.

record.verdict_notes: Even if teacher accuracies had been reported, the setup differs from the original weak-to-strong recipe: the student sees ground-truth labels in half its loss, so any student-above-teacher result would not isolate generalization from weak supervision. The text gives the EfficientNet B4 size as both 22.28% (Table 3) and 22.82% (Section 3.4). No uncertainty estimates are reported, and the runs use a single seed (42) and only 10 epochs.

versions.untested_parts: No weak-supervisor performance or PGR is reported; student performance is not compared with the weak teacher's task performance.
Soft and hard distillation are compared on task accuracy, but not on PGR against naive fine-tuning.
Teacher and student sizes and downstream datasets vary, but the study does not measure PGR or its predictors.
No supervisor-checkability gap, distribution shift, or shared-error analysis is reported.
No theoretical conditions for beating a supervisor are analyzed.
The setting is computer vision, but no direct comparison of student performance with weak-supervisor performance establishes the claimed effect outside language.
